High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Nilesh Patel, Advocate for the petitioner [P-1].

Shri Madhusudan Yadav, Govt. Advocate for the responden Heard on I.A. No.17747/2023, which is an application seeking permission to obtain passport for travelling to Mecca, Saudi Arabia for pilgrimage(Umrah).

The revision petitioner has filed the present criminal revision petition u/S 397 read with Section 401 of Cr.P.C., being aggrieved by the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 07.07.2014,
passed by the learned XIVth Additional Sessions Judge, Indore, Distt. Indore(M.P.) in Cri.A.
No.525/2010 by which petitioner stood convicted for an offence punishable u/S 7(1) read with Section 16(1)(a) of The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and has been sentenced to undergo 06 months Rigorous Imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,500/- affirming the judgment dated 20.09.2010, passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Indore in Criminal Case No.21520/2010, with default stipulation.
Learned counsel for the petitioner - Tarab Khan submits that during the pendency of the present revision, the petitioner has moved an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
The jail sentence of the petitioner has already been suspended by co-ordinate Bench of this Court 2 CRR-750-2014 vide order dated 10.07.2014 and he has not misused the liberty granted to him.
Learned counsel further submits that revision petitioner desires to visit Mecca, Saudi Arabia, for pilgrimage (Umrah).

Though the petitioner has filed an application for issuance of passport, but the Passport Authority has kept the application of petitioner on hold on the ground that petitioner is first required to seek necessary permission from this Court as per the notification dated 25.08.1993 issued by the Ministry of External Affairs.
Hence, necessary permission be granted in the light of notification dated 25.08.1993 for obtaining/issuance of passport to the petitioner for a period of one year in the interest of justice.
Learned counsel for respondent/State has opposes the prayer for grant of permission for issuance of passport to the petitioner in view of pendency of the present criminal revision.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Admittedly, revision petitioner has been convicted, therefore, as per Section 6(2) of the Indian Passport Act, 1967, passport authority has the power to refuse issuance of the passport in view of the pendency of the criminal revision filed by the petitioner.

However, as per the notification dated 25.08.1993, passport may be issued on production of an order by the concerned Court permitting the petitioner to obtain passport and depart from India on conditions, as stipulated thereunder.

Since the sentence of petitioner had already been suspended by co- ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 10.07.2014 and petitioner has 3 CRR-750-2014 not misused the liberty so granted, I.A.
No. 17747/2023 deserves to be allowed.
The Passport Authority is permitted to issue passport to the petitioner - Torab/Tarab Khan , as per provisions of the Indian Passport Act, 1967 for a period of one year.
I.A. No.17747/2023 stands disposed of accordingly.

(SANJEEV S KALGAONKAR) JUDGE pn Tarab Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74048467/
